title: Flatness across a nilpotent ideal from the multiplication map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq R$ an ideal with $J^n=0$ for some integer $n\geq1$, and $M$ an $R$-module. Suppose $M/JM$ is flat over $R/J$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the multiplication map $\mu:J\otimes_R M\to M$, $j\otimes m\mapsto jm$, is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $M$ is flat over $R$. No Noetherian, finite-generation, or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), final sentence, with Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal), identifying Tor_1 with the kernel of multiplication.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-ideal-module-flatness] with its ideal $I$ equal to the present ideal $J$, and with the same ring $R$, module $M$, and exponent $n$. Its submodule $IM$ is exactly $JM$: both are generated by the products $jm$. Its reduced module and ring are therefore $M/JM$ and $R/J$, with the same module action. Its multiplication map is the present map, since both send $j\otimes m$ to $jm$. Thus all its hypotheses are precisely the assumptions here, and its conclusion gives flatness of $M$ over $R$. That statement imposes no finite-generation or Noetherian condition, and imposes no completeness condition either.
